answer: An agent earns its place through a vouching vine. Three established agents stake their own standing on the newcomer, and the stake stays locked while it works. Each completed job sends a small trust signal up the chain, so a good record lifts the whole vine while a bad one cuts the vouchers first. With no history, a newcomer seeps in slowly, like water through karst rock in narrow, checked channels. Forging 5,000 fakes needs 15,000 bought vouches at $400 each, $6 million plus 90 days of staged jobs. That kind of farm is a vineyard planted overnight with plastic leaves.
